newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuban Justice Minister Amat dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Cuban Justice Minister Amat dismissed.

text.p: Cuban Justice Minister Carlos Amat has been dismissed from his post, the ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma said on Friday.
A brief item said the Council of State, which is headed by President Fidel Castro, had approved the replacement of Amat with Roberto Diaz Sotolongo.
Sotolongo was deputy head of the organisational department of the Communist Party's Central Committee.
Granma gave no reason for Amat's dismissal.
It also did not say if Amat had been given a new job and, unusually for such cases, it did not praise Amat's work at the Justice Ministry. This suggested the Cuban leadership was unhappy with him.
Amat took over the post as Justice Minister in 1990, replacing now state prosecutor Juan Escalona. Until then Amat had been deputy minister at the Justice Ministry.
The change of posts was the first in the Cuban government this year.
